detail.extracted_title: Global Muscat Plan Forum Unites Leaders from 40 Countries in Oman | OmanSpire
detail.instagram_caption:
Religious and traditional leaders, Indigenous representatives, United Nations officials, policymakers, and young peacebuilders from 40 countries have gathered in the Omani capital for the Global Muscat Plan Forum, hosted by the Sultanate of Oman through the Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs.

Coinciding with the International Day for Tolerance, the two-day consultative meeting brings together 70 participants around a clear premise: sustainable peace cannot rely on political agreements alone. Opening the forum, His Excellency Dr Mohammed bin Said Al Maamari called for institutional legitimacy to work alongside community trust, pairing specialised policy mechanisms with inherited local wisdom to detect early warning signs and counter hate speech before tensions escalate.

Launched at United Nations Headquarters in New York in June 2026 following consultations across 38 countries, the Muscat Plan is now moving into a measurable implementation framework built on capacity-building, constructive dialogue, and cross-generational cooperation—from former heads of state and Indigenous elders to young mediators from more than 20 countries and schoolchildren in Muscat defining tolerance in their own words.

Read more on omanspire.om (link in bio).

p: Hosted in Muscat by the [[Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs]], the Global Muscat Plan Forum brings together [[70 participants from 40 countries]]—uniting religious and traditional leaders, {{Indigenous representatives, UN officials, and youth}} against hate speech and mass atrocities.

slides.h: Peace begins long before conflict erupts.

quote.text: What we need today is for the legitimacy of institutions to complement the trust of communities, and for specialised knowledge to come together with inherited wisdom.

slides.h: Three pillars moving the Muscat Plan into practice.
brief: Equipping [[community and traditional leaders]] with practical tools to spot early warning signs and defuse emerging tensions.
Promoting constructive {{interfaith and cross-cultural dialogue}} before divisive rhetoric turns neighbours into enemies.
Connecting [[Indigenous Peoples, women, and youth]] with governments and UN bodies through the {{Muscat Process}}.

slides.h: From UN headquarters to classrooms in Muscat.
p: Launched at the [[United Nations on 11 June 2026]] after consultations across {{38 countries}}, the initiative pairs elders and former heads of state with [[young peacebuilders from 20+ nations]] and Muscat schoolchildren—grounding global diplomacy in everyday coexistence.
